findings.finding: On Hyper-V the init runs read_keys over /proc/cmdline and then over the relay seed into the same variables, so a seed key silently overrides the same command-line key and a command-line key the seed omits is kept: a per-key merge of two boot channels. The design's Defaults and overrides says 'the seed and the command line never both supply a key (Hyper-V reads the seed's values)' and names no merge. Today it has no effect (the UKI command line is 'console=ttyS0 console=tty0' and warden's seed writes every key), but the code lets a seed with no claim_token run with one from the command line.
findings.fix: On Hyper-V take the keys from the seed only: stop with a console line when /proc/cmdline carries a warden.* key (naming it), or skip the command-line read_keys when HYPERV=1. Add a driver/relayvm/init_test.go case.
findings.resolution: Fixed in e53b12e: on Hyper-V the init no longer reads /proc/cmdline's keys (read_keys over it runs only in the else branch), and a warden.* word on the Hyper-V command line stops the init before the seed is read, naming the key ('stopped: warden.<key> on the kernel command line: on Hyper-V the relay seed (WARDENRELAY) alone carries the boot keys'). TestRelayInitHyperVSeedAlone pins the branch shape and the refusal's order; README and overview.md pseudocode updated (FLOW-15). The refusal is not a default or merge, so nothing new to list in Defaults and overrides.

findings.finding: Setup passes no DevNAT, so EnsureNetwork takes any NAT that owns the --nat-prefix, whatever its name (another build's per-build NAT, or a non-warden NAT). Setup then prints 'Durable dev network ready' naming it. VerifyNetwork reads only <network>-nat (netProbeScript with no otherPrefix), so every durable build is refused with 'the durable network's NAT "warden-dev-nat" is missing', and its fix ('run warden setup') succeeds again without changing anything. The user loops. On main, VerifyNetwork checked only the Private switch. Decision 5 says the durable strategy uses <switch>-nat. (Pre-review candidate 7, confirmed.)
findings.fix: In RunSetup, refuse (driver.Fixable) when res.NATName is not <network>-nat, naming the NAT that owns the prefix and how to remove it or choose another --nat-prefix, so that setup succeeds only on a NAT durable builds accept. Pin it with a pure test of the setup decision.
findings.resolution: Fixed in aff6ffd: RunSetup goes through ensureSetupNAT, which refuses (driver.Fixable) a NAT whose name is not <network>-nat that owns the prefix, naming it, the NAT durable builds use, and the fix (remove it once nothing uses it, or pass another --nat-prefix). EnsureNetwork only adopts in that case, so the refusal comes before setup changes anything. TestSetupRefusesNATDurableBuildsReject pins the three cases with a fake Provisioner; cli.md and overview.md updated (UX-01, FLOW-15).

findings.finding: New behavior: when CollectorTransport is nil, a direct CollectorURL that names a host dials through the relay's resolver list (a cloned default transport with upstreamDialContext). No test covers it: every relay test sets CollectorTransport or uses an IP or placeholder URL. warden's drivers use the tunnel, so only third-party claimants reach this path, but it is the relay's only output path (RELAY-07). (Pre-review candidate 8b, confirmed.)
findings.fix: Add a relay test: CollectorURL http://collector.example:<port> with no CollectorTransport, a fake resolver from upstream_dns_test.go that answers 127.0.0.1, and a check that the collector receives the sink's request and the resolver was asked.

findings.finding: F2's report reads 'installed' only from a successful OpenService. Any OpenService error other than ERROR_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST returns installed=false, so doctor prints 'Privileged service ... not installed', the VM lifecycle and network remedies and Ready's reason say 'install the network service', and only the Probe notes carry 'privileged service state: open service WardenHyperV: Access is denied.' That is the native F2 symptom on a failed read: an unread state taken as absent, a path that runs only on failure and that task 52 rules out ('never "not installed"'). It is reachable: WardenHyperV's DACL on this host (sc sdshow) is D:(A;;CCLCSWRPWPDTLOCRRC;;;SY)(A;;CCDCLCSWRPWPDTLOCRSDRCWDWO;;;BA)(A;;CCLCSWLOCRRC;;;IU)(A;;CCLCSWLOCRRC;;;SU), the CreateService default warden installs with, so SERVICE_QUERY_STATUS is granted to interactive (IU) and service (SU) logons only. A non-elevated warden in an SSH (network) or Task Scheduler run-whether-logged-on (batch) session with the service stopped gets 'not installed' and the install remedy, and `warden hyperv service install` then refuses because the service is registered. The QueryServiceStatus failure path already does the right thing (installed, 'in an unknown state'). servicestate_test.go has no read-error case.
findings.fix: Do not turn a failed SCM read into 'not installed'. ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED from OpenService means the SCM resolved the name (it reports ERROR_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST first), so record the service as installed with its state unread; for any other error record the state as unread (a third value, not installed=false), print the row as 'state unread: <err>' and name neither install nor start as certain (for example: from an elevated shell, `sc query WardenHyperV`; start it if stopped, install it if absent). Add the read-error rows to TestServiceRowStates.
findings.resolution: Fixed in cee4721 (task 56): queryService's answer goes through scmServiceState, where only ERROR_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST is not installed; access denied is installed with the state unread; any other error leaves it unread. Detect records the error in Capabilities.ServiceUnread (no longer only in the probe notes). Doctor prints 'installed, but its state could not be read (<err>)' or 'state could not be read (<err>)', and the row, the VM lifecycle and network remedies and Ready name `Get-Service WardenHyperV` from an elevated shell (start it if stopped; install it only if absent, and only when the SCM did not find the name). TestServiceRowStates' access-denied and read-failed rows assert that the install remedy never appears in the output or Ready's reason. An OpenSCManager failure also lands in ServiceUnread. cli.md, drivers.md and overview.md updated.

findings.finding: The prefix-mismatch refusal moved into ensureSetupNAT unchanged: it still compares against opts.NATPrefix after applyDefaults, so it fires when --nat-prefix was never passed. Re-running 'warden setup --driver hyperv --slots 8' on a host set up with --nat-prefix 10.200.0.0/24 is refused 'not --nat-prefix 192.168.240.0/20', naming a flag the user did not pass and telling them to delete their NAT. The design does not name this refusal, and Decision 5 has builds use the dev NAT 'whatever prefix setup gave it'. --host-ip is still not compared, so an explicit --host-ip that differs from an existing NAT's is silently not used. The new M2 refusal has the same wording shape ('already owns --nat-prefix <default>') but is correct either way, since another NAT on the prefix does break durable builds.
findings.fix: Compare only flags the user gave: refuse an explicit --nat-prefix or --host-ip that differs from the existing <network>-nat, and without them adopt the existing NAT and print what was read back.

findings.finding: Dropping 'the hyperv driver's default NAT' from linkRanges (F3) is right for a host whose NAT is elsewhere, but it moves the refusal of a link inside 192.168.240.0/20 on a host with no NAT yet from config load to after the seed ISO (line 76) and the network standup: the ephemeral and service paths call EnsureNetwork, which makes a per-build Private switch and a per-build NAT on the default prefix (provisionBuildNetwork), and only then prepareBuildNetwork (108) refuses, and the deferred cleanup tears them down. UX-04 item 2 puts a cheap check before a network standup. The check is correct and names its fix, and the approved flow already ran it after the standup for a read-back NAT, so this is SHOULD: r4 routes one more case there, the one load used to catch at once.
findings.fix: Before buildSeed and the standup, run checkNATOverlap against the NAT the build would use, read back without standing anything up (doctor's netReadback already does this: the durable resources, the dev switch's NAT, or the default prefix when there is none); keep the post-standup check as the one against the NAT actually taken. Or, at least, check the default prefix before EnsureNetwork when the read-back finds no NAT.
findings.resolution: Fixed in 24d096d (task 58): StartBuild calls preflightBuild before the per-build lock, the disks and the seed ISO. It reads the NAT back with netProbeScript as doctor does (durable: <network>-nat only; otherwise the dev switch's NAT, the one owning the default prefix, or none), and checkLinkAhead runs checkNATOverlap on natAhead's choice, naming the default prefix when the host has none. The check after the standup stays, against the NAT actually taken. Doctor's writeNAT shares natAhead, so build and doctor choose the same way. TestCheckLinkAhead covers ephemeral (no NAT, host NAT) and durable (in the NAT, no slots) with a link inside and outside. The cost is one PowerShell read-back at build start, the same kind of probe Detect already runs.
